questions.do: Make any kundli, then read the Your lagna card and The sky when you were born.
questions.a: The rashi that was rising on the eastern horizon at the moment and place of birth. It changes about every two hours, which is why the birth time and place matter so much.

questions.q: Why can two people born on the same day in different cities have different lagnas but the same Moon sign?
questions.do: Make a kundli, then change only the Place of birth and compare the lagna and Moon sign.
questions.a: The Moon’s position in the sky is the same for everyone at one moment, but which part of the sky is rising depends on where you stand on the turning Earth.

questions.q: How wide is one nakshatra, and how many are there?
questions.do: Open See the full kundli and look at the nakshatra column.

questions.q: What does the page check its Sun calculation against?
questions.do: Open For experts: how accurate is this? at the bottom.
questions.a: The dates of Makar Sankranti (14 January) and Mesha Sankranti (13 or 14 April), when the Sun enters sidereal Makara and Mesha.

questions.q: Why does the page warn when a placement is close to a border?
questions.do: Make a kundli and read the yellow or green box under your result cards.
questions.a: Birth times are often rounded to 5 or 10 minutes. If the lagna or a graha is within a few minutes of changing rashi or nakshatra, the recorded time cannot settle it.
